Sustained by the Standard-Bearer's brand. While the bearer lives, this thrall fights without fear or pain. Cut down the bearer to sever the Mark.
Mark of the Absolute
The Standard-Bearer's brand reaches every thrall within 9m, holding the puppets to their will.

That's far enough. We've buried enough friends today without adding a stranger who lingers.
I only came to help.
You're outnumbered. You should run.
Help. Everyone's got help, right up until they've got a knife. But you did stand with us, or near enough. So. Thanks. Now let me grieve in peace.
Run. That's what got half of Elturel eaten. We ran all the way here. This dirt's as good as any to plant our feet, and them. Move along, adventurer. We hold.
Gods be good: alive! We're alive! And you, friend: hale, armed, and clearly a person of taste and means.
Terrible thing, an ambush. Wonderful thing, a customer.
Since we're both still breathing, might I interest you in a little... commerce? Everything's for sale except the wheels.
Third fight this tenday. I started keeping the count on my spear-haft. I'm running out of haft.
You watched us bleed before you decided we were worth knowing. Don't fret; everyone weighs the odds now. Just don't expect me to turn my back.
Every one of them wears that brand like it's a blessing. I put an arrow in one today and she smiled at me while she bled. Smiled.
Hells. My hands only started shaking now that it's over. That's normal, right? ...That's normal.
I fletched arrows for goose hunts, before all this. Geese. Now look at me.
I felt it when they fell: something let go of them, like a hand opening. Gods don't let go that easily.
I have watched a century of bad omens come and go. This is the first one that marches in formation.
Fifty years in this work, and the worst part never changes: the burying. The fighting's over in minutes. The burying takes all day.
Three bolts, three of theirs. I'd call that arithmetic, not heroism.
Don't stand so close, friend. The last stranger who watched us fight that calmly turned out to be counting our arrows.
Their minds were... quiet. All of them, the same quiet. Like ten instruments holding one note. I set fire to it, and even burning, it hummed.
The crows won't touch them. They circle all day and land on everything else. Even the carrion knows something's wrong with that meat.
The job was 'walk the road, guard the crates'. Nobody priced in a holy war. There's a renegotiation coming.
I've been shot at by rivals, guards, and one very committed goose. This lot's the first that didn't flinch. Unnatural.
Save the questions. Answers cost coin, and today's stock got blood on it.
They don't scream right, you know. Hit a man, he screams for himself. These scream like it's on somebody else's behalf.
Counterspelled one mid-prayer. Whatever answered him wasn't a god. Gods have better diction.
First time I ever swung this at something that swung back. Trees never bled, neither. I'm going to have opinions about that tonight.
My grandfather's axe, this. Cut roofs, cradles, one wedding table. Suppose it cuts history now, too.
The saw pit's ruined, the mule's run off, and my hands won't stop shaking. But the cart's fine! The cart's fine.
I know these woods better than my own house. Whatever they were marching toward, it isn't on any map I've ever walked.
They looked at my horns and called me 'kin'. Kin! I chop wood, you dead-eyed lunatics.
We already ran from one war. I planted a garden here. Carrots. This was going to be the year I had carrots.
Everyone keeps saying 'militia' like it's a thing we are. It's a bell and a shed with spears in it. That's the whole militia.
I hid in the well. I'm not ashamed. From down there the whole battle was boots and yelling, and then quiet. The quiet was worse.
My da held this door in the plague year. I held it today. Doors, apparently. That's our family's entire war.
They didn't shout 'attack' or 'charge' or anything at all. They just... started. All at once. Like one thing wearing thirty bodies.
Everyone forgets the small guard until somebody's hamstrung. Then it's all 'oh, THERE you are'.
The trick is to watch their feet, not their eyes. These had it backwards: dead eyes, sure feet. I don't enjoy learning new tricks mid-fight.
The client pays for the escort and gets the miracle free of charge. Today the miracle did the heavy lifting.
Two hundred years of trade and I have never once died. Today the record held. Barely. Come, look: everything survived except my nerves.
You know what survives an ambush? Inventory, friend. Inventory and optimism. Both happen to be for sale.
You saw nothing here worth repeating, stranger. A road, a fight, some corpses. That's the whole story.
You're Harpers, aren't you?
Who were they?
I said you saw nothing. ...But you've a good ear. Every one of these dead took that brand willingly. That's what keeps me up at night. Not the dying. The volunteering.
Fanatics wearing somebody's mark. There's a ledger somewhere with all their names crossed out, and the hand that crossed them isn't done writing.
Well. You're either a witness or a customer, and I don't pay witnesses.
You're Zhentarim.
Why would cultists attack mercenaries?
And you say it like it means trouble. Today it means the only armed company on this road that pays its debts. Those fanatics cost me two contracts and a good hat.
Because their Absolute doesn't buy; it takes. Bad for business, worse for the taken. We shoot back on principle. The principle is called 'margin'.
HA! Alive! Twelve years felling oaks, and it turns out the swing works just the same on... whatever those were.
You handled yourselves well.
What happened here?
We handled ourselves TERRIBLY, friend. That's the miracle of it. Berk over there threw his axe. THREW it. It worked! Nobody tell him it shouldn't have.
We were cutting timber. They came out of the treeline with that look, like the forest owed them something. Well. The forest had axes in it.
It's over? It's... over. I can't tell anymore. My ears are still in the middle of it.
Are you hurt?
You fought well.
No. No, that's the strange part: not a scratch. My neighbour took a spear that was meant for me, and I don't even remember his face doing it. Just his hands.
I closed my eyes on the second swing. Whatever I hit, I hit it with my eyes closed. Don't tell the others.
Cargo's intact. Client's breathing. Everything else about today can hang.
You're paid guards?
Rough fight?
Paid, yes. 'Guard' got ambitious today. The contract covers bandits, wolves, and 'acts of weather'. Fanatics with a brand are going in the next draft.
Nine years I've walked this road. It never once fought back before. Roads are supposed to be the boring part.

Absolute's Attention I
The Absolute barely registers your existence. Occasional patrols sweep the region.
Absolute's Attention II
Your strikes have been noticed. The Absolute's warbands now march with devout supporters.
Absolute's Attention III
The Absolute has ordered your hunt. Events grow more frequent; warriors reinforce every band.
Absolute's Attention IV
You are a priority target. Shock bugbears escort the warbands.
Absolute's Attention V
The Absolute's full wrath. Intellect devourers stalk beside every band sent after you.
Peace, stranger, or as much of it as this road allows. We walk to a shrine three days on. The road tests the faithful; today it tested us harder than most.
You're pilgrims?
What were they?
Armed ones, now. Faith didn't put the staff in my hand; the road did that. But faith's what kept it steady when they came. I'll not complain about the bargain.

Devotion, turned wrong. They wore their god's mark like a wound they were proud of. I've knelt to a god my whole life and never once wanted to bleed for the pleasure of it. That's the difference, and it's the whole of it.
I prayed the entire time: not for rescue, for steadiness. The steadiness came. I'll let the priests argue over what that means. I'm just grateful my hands stopped shaking before the second wave.
My god is patient and carved from mountain-stone. Whatever theirs is, it's in a dreadful hurry: marching, branding, devouring. Age teaches you to distrust anything holy that's in a rush.
The shrine's still three days on. Three days lighter now, without the two we left in the mud. We'll carry their names the rest of the way. A pilgrimage can hold a few more prayers.
Surface is loud. That was louder. I'll take a cave-in over that any day; at least a cave-in doesn't pray while it kills you.
You're a long way from the Underdark.
You fight well, for a gnome.
Ironhand doesn't scatter without a reason. The reason's up here now, wearing a brand and calling it faith. We came up to breathe. Turns out the air up here bites too.
Small target, sharp knife, low expectations. That's three advantages you great tall folk never learn. Everyone always forgets the knees, and everyone always regrets it.
Down below you learn to shoot at the shine of eyes in the dark. These ones' eyes didn't shine right: flat, like a fish on ice. Aimed a hand's-width low out of habit and hit anyway. Small mercies.
Flaming Fist. We hold the line, even out here, even when the line's just mud and the two of us left standing on it.
You're a long way from Baldur's Gate.
Rough fight?

The city's reach is longer than its walls; that's the whole idea of us. Somebody's got to stand on the roads so the roads stay roads. Today that somebody was us. Tomorrow, gods willing, it's a bigger company and a shorter shift.
Every fight's rough when the other side doesn't fear dying. Discipline beats fervor most days; costs you, but it beats it. Cost us two today. The line held. Same as it always does.

You want to know why the Fist doesn't run? On a day like this it's not the city, whatever the oath says. It's the poor fool bleeding on your left, who dies the moment you turn. You hold for them. Everything else is just what it says on the report.

You train on straw butts and drunk bandits. Nothing trains you for one of them who takes a bolt to the chest and keeps walking. So I put a second one in it. Then a third. Marksmanship's just persistence with better aim.
Back in the city this'd be a bad night's watch and a worse morning report. Out here it's the whole war, and no relief coming till dawn. If dawn's still on the roster.
Stand easy, stranger. The Even-Handed sees the brand for what it is, and so, now, do you. Justice was done here, though it took a hard hand to do it.
You serve Tyr?
Was it worth it?
I swore to stand between the cruel and the wronged. I don't get to choose the day the cruel arrive, or how many. The oath doesn't shrink to fit an easier fight. So I stood, and I'd stand again.
Two of ours lie here. I weigh them against the oath, as Tyr weighs all things: by the deed, not the feeling. The deed was just. It doesn't make the weight lighter. It only makes it bearable.

Some knights swing for glory. Some swing for grief. I try to swing for neither, only the gap between the cruel and the wronged, kept clear one more day. Vengeance is a fire. The oath is a wall. Walls are duller. Walls hold.

Tyr is blind, they say, so he judges by the weight of the deed, never the face that wears it. I judged these, and struck, and my sleep tonight will be dreamless. That is the gift of a clean conscience: it asks no questions in the dark.
I gave three of them their last rites even as I traded blows: mercy for the soul, steel for the body. The Maimed God asks both of me, and I do not get to choose which is easier. Neither is.
You're staring. Everyone stares. Yes: a drow, above ground, with her blade pointed at the Absolute's dogs instead of yours. The world's stranger than your prejudices, outlander.
Most of your kind serve something.
You're a surface drow now?

Most of my kind serve a spider who eats her own. I cut that thread a century ago, and I did not climb all this way toward the sun to slip a new leash over my own head. One god's cruelty was educational enough.

I belong to no one and nowhere: too dark for the sun, too sun-touched for the deep. It's a lonely country, freedom. But it's mine, and I bled for it today same as any of these poor sods bled for their little farms.

A hundred years I spent making a bow do precisely what I tell it: no goddess, no whip, no brand whispering in the ear. That's the only obedience I keep now: the arrow's, to me. Turns out it's enough to build a life on.

They cut down a grove and think it's a victory. Root remembers. Seed remembers. Give this road ten years and it is thorn and bramble, and every mark they burned is a bark-scar swallowed whole. The wild does not lose to the likes of them. It only waits, and it has never once been in a hurry.

Three of the circle walked out with me this morning. The oak we planted the day I took my vows still stands. I cannot say the same of the three. Nature keeps a cruel ledger: it always balances, never when you'd ask it to.
You're a druid?
Who were they?

Of the old circle, yes. We don't march. We don't conquer. We tend: we splint the snapped bough, we bury the fallen deer. But you cannot tend a thing that walks in burning while it prays. So today I did the other thing a druid can do. I am not proud of how well it came to my hand.

Grief wearing a god's face. They came branded and singing, hollow behind the eyes, and they left my circle-kin cold in the leaf-litter. I gave them back to the earth the way I would any dead creature. The earth doesn't care what killed them. Only I do.

Silvanus asks one thing of us: keep the balance. Predator and prey, fire and green, the turn of the season. Then a thing arrives that belongs to no turning, that only takes and brands and names the taking holy. A predator is hungry, stranger, and then it is full. That was never going to be full. So I stood against it, balance be damned. Sometimes keeping the balance means being the weight that tips it back.

You'll want your lantern close and your voice low out here, stranger. The dark isn't just dark: it's hungry, and older than the thing that woke it. We nearly joined the ones who walk without light. Nearly.
You're a Harper?
What's out here worth guarding?

The Harpers watch, mostly: roads, rumors, the quiet before a bad thing. But there's no watching this from a safe distance; the curse doesn't respect the observer. So we carry light and steel both, and we walk the roads no one else will. Someone has to know what's coming down them.

A road. One road, to one inn, with one light still burning at the end of it. Everything the curse hasn't swallowed is crowded under that light now. Cut the road and you cut the last artery. That's what they mean to do. That's what we don't let them.

I have watched two hundred winters. None were this dark. The shadow here doesn't fall; it reaches. I keep my lantern between it and my skin and remind myself that even the longest night in the histories broke into morning eventually. This one will too. I may not see it. The morning doesn't need me to.

You learn to shoot by lantern-light out here; everything past the ring of it is guesswork and prayer. I loose at the sounds, mostly: a wet step, a wrong branch. I hope the thing making them wished me harm. Most did. The curse doesn't leave many friendly things in the dark.

Luck ran out of this land a long time ago, so I don't rely on it. I've squeezed through gaps taller Harpers died in front of, staying low and quiet and lit while the dark went looking for easier prey. It's not cleverness and it's not courage. It's just refusing to be the one it catches.

They say the dead here don't rest; they just work for whoever cursed the ground. I've seen shapes wearing Harper pins shamble past that had no business still walking. I took the pins back. Someone should remember they were ours before they were the dark's.

Guardian's a heavy word. Mostly it means I stand where the line is thinnest and I do not move. Held a bridge alone once for the length of a hymn. Held this road today for less time and it cost more. The line held. Ask me what it cost and I'll change the subject.

Light is a spell out here and also a religion: cast it wrong and you die, believe in it too little and you die. I keep a flame in my palm and my doubt behind my teeth. The dark tests both. Today it tested them hard, and both held. Tomorrow's a fresh examination.

Commander, they call me, which mostly means I decide who stands where the dark is thickest. I decided today. Two of the people I decided for won't be walking back. That's the job. It doesn't get lighter with rank. It gets heavier.
You lead the Harpers here?
Can this land be saved?

This cell of them. We're the eyes on the road between the last light and the worst dark. Moonrise sits at one end of it like a spider; everything we love is huddled at the other. I command the thread of road between. A very short command, and a very long war.

Saved? I don't plan that far. I plan to the next lantern, the next mile, the next dawn we manufacture ourselves out of oil and refusal. Save the land is a story for people who live to tell it. First we keep a road open. I intend to be one of the ones who tell it. No promises.

From up high you see it all: the dark moving like water, the lantern-lines of the living, the places where the light's gone out for good. I'm a sentinel. My whole purpose is to see the bad thing before it arrives. Today I saw it and still couldn't stop it arriving. Seeing isn't stopping.
You watch from above?
What did you see coming?

The high ground, the ridgelines, the old towers. Aerial, they call us, though none of us fly; we just climb where we can see farthest, lanterns lit against the dark, and count what's coming. Numbers, direction, how much light they carry. Then we loose arrows and send word. The word matters more than the arrows. Arrows only kill what's already here.

More than yesterday. Always more than yesterday. The dark end of the road is patient and well-supplied, and every day the lantern-lines on my map grow shorter. I don't report that part to the ones below. They carry enough. I carry the map alone.

I loosed my last arrow at a shape three ridgelines out, and I'll go to my grave not knowing if it landed, and that isn't the worst thing I'll never know out here. The perch is cold. The nights are long and lonely, and the dark keeps its own counsel. Still I climb up, and I watch. Someone has to be the eyes.

Selûne is the moon, and the moon is the one thing this cursed sky can't fully swallow. I wear her silver and I stand where her light still falls, and where it doesn't, I carry my own. A knight of the Moonmaiden doesn't wait for dawn. In a place like this, dawn might not come. So you become the light, or you become the dark. I made my choice at my vows.

They fell on us in the dark, thinking the dark was their ally. But I was raised by moonlight and I fight best in it: every shadow they hid in, I already knew the shape of. Silver in one hand, the Moonmaiden's grace in the other. Two of them learned that the dark is not always a friend to the ones who serve its master.

Peace of the Moonmaiden on you, such peace as this benighted place allows. I tend the wounded and I bless the fallen, and today I did far more of the second than I would ever choose. Selûne teaches that even the darkest night is only the moon turned away. I hold to that. Some nights I hold to it with both hands.
You serve Selûne?
Does the moon really watch this place?

Her priestess, yes, out here where her light is needed most and reaches least. The curse is a wound in the world, and a wound needs tending, not conquering. So I mend what I can, light what I can, and sing the fallen toward a moon they can no longer see. Small work against a vast dark. Small work is still work.

She watches. Whether she can reach, that is the harder question, and I won't lie to the grieving by pretending I know. What I know is that her light hasn't gone out in me, and while it burns in even one of us, this land is not wholly lost. I intend to be very hard to extinguish.

Kelemvor keep you, and keep you the RIGHT way, in the ground and at rest, not shambling upright the way this cursed earth insists. That is my quarrel here, stranger. Not conquest. The dead are being denied their door, and I am a doorkeeper by holy office.
You're a priest of the dead?
Can you undo the curse?

Of the Lord of the Dead, yes, not the morbid thing folk imagine. Kelemvor's mercy is the full stop at the end of a life. Rest. An ending that stays ended. This land steals that ending, props the dead back up, marches them. Every corpse that walks here is a theft from my god's hall. I came to close doors that were forced open.

Undo it? No. But I can give one soul at a time its proper rest, and refuse to let the ones I loved be turned into the very thing we fight. When they fall, when I fall, someone must be there to make the ending stick. That is the whole of my ministry out here. It is enough to die for. I may yet prove it.

A warden guards a boundary. Mine's the one between the dead who rest and the dead who don't. Sounds like priest's work, and it is; but priests need someone with a mace to hold the line while they pray. That's me. I've put down more than I want to count today, and I whispered Kelemvor's leave over every one who fell. They were people first. They deserve the words.

We ran from one burning place straight into a dark one; that's the refugee's luck. Out of the fire and into the shadow. I'm no soldier. I'm a hedge-mage who learned three battle-cantrips on the road because the road demanded it. They kept us alive to the next mile. Barely.
Where are you fleeing to?
You fought them off yourself?

The light at the end of the road, same as everyone. Somewhere ahead, they say. Somewhere safe. Half of us stopped believing 'safe' points at anything real; we walk toward it anyway. A rumor of safety is still more than the certainty behind us. Tieflings have practice living on rumors of safety.

Myself, three cantrips, and a great deal of luck I'd rather not spend again. I set my hands alight, remembered every cruel thing anyone ever called my kind, and gave the fire to the ones in our way. It isn't heroism, stranger. It's just a tiefling refusing, one more time, to die quietly because something decided we should.

I carried a child and a quiver on the same shoulder for six miles and couldn't tell you which was heavier by the end. Put down two of them without setting either burden down. You don't choose your strength: the road chooses it for you, then it takes everything you've got. The child's under the light now. The quiver's empty. Fair trade.

You're looking at a dead man who forgot to lie down. They had me in a cell under Moonrise: you don't come back from those, everyone knows it. I came back. I don't recommend the method and I can't fully explain the luck. But I'm out, I'm armed, and I am never going back down those stairs alive.
You escaped Moonrise?
What did they do to you down there?

The prison beneath it. They take you down for the gift; that's what they call the thing they put in your skull. I got out before my turn. Left friends on those stairs who weren't quick enough. I hear them some nights, the ones who got the gift. That's the worst of it: they're still down there, and they've stopped screaming. That's how you know it's too late for them.

To me? Not enough. To the others, more than a mouth should say out loud. I've decided not to say it: saying it makes it a memory instead of a nightmare, and I'm not ready to be calm about it yet. Maybe when this is over. Under a real sky, I could tell it all. If there's a then.

I counted the days in that cell by the screaming: it came in shifts, regular as a bell. When my shift got close, I stopped counting and started digging. Got out with these two hands and a spoon's worth of luck. Every shadow since has looked like a guard coming to drag me back, so I swing first now, guard or not. I'll apologize to the innocent ones in the next life, assuming this curse lets anyone have one.

Flaming Fist. Or I was, when there was a Fist to be part of out here. Now I'm a uniform with no chain of command, walking a road with a sword and a habit of standing my ground. Old habits are all that's left. They'll do.
The Fist retreated?
Where are you headed?

The Fist broke. There's a difference, and I'll die insisting on it. We didn't run; we were scattered, cut off, swallowed by the dark in ones and twos until there was no 'we' left to give the order to fall back. I'm what washed up. A soldier without an army is just a stubborn man with a sword. But a stubborn man with a sword still counts for one road held an hour longer.

The light. Same as everyone crawling this road, though I want more than a warm room out of it. Give a soldier a post and a wall that still stands, and I'll hold it till it falls. A soldier needs something to hold, or he's just a man rusting in a dented breastplate. I'll find a new wall, or make the road my wall until then.

I've got maybe six arrows and no idea where the next six come from. The quartermaster's dead, the supply line's a memory, and the dark doesn't take requisition forms. So I make each shot a decision instead of a habit. Six arrows, six choices. It's a strange way to soldier. It's the only way left out here.

The Absolute hunts you for the whole campaign. Every option here is read live: changing it takes effect on the very next long rest, and the choice is stored in your save. Hover an option to read exactly what it changes.

The master switch for the whole encounter engine. On, every long rest rolls for an event: 20 percent at low Attention, rising to 40 percent once you have killed seven commanders, plus 20 more for each silent night in a row. Off, that roll still happens but nothing is ever dispatched. Warbands already in the world keep behaving normally, corpses still clean up, and a commander that already fled still comes back.

Battles between the Absolute and the Resistance where you start neutral and may watch, join either side, or walk away. They are 37 of every 100 events. Turned off, that share becomes patrols instead of empty nights, so the total number of encounters does not drop.

A commander that drops to 30 percent health flees the field instead of dying. It returns at a later encounter with a name of its own, full health, magical gear, a title, and resistance to the damage types you used against it. Turned off, commanders fight to the death and nothing is ever queued for revenge.

How often the army finds you after a long rest. This shifts the base chance of every Attention band at once, so the escalation curve keeps its shape. A quieter setting also means longer silences, because the pressure that builds on empty nights starts from a lower floor.
Ten points below the shipped curve. Encounters start around one night in ten and you can go four nights without seeing anyone.
The shipped balance, tuned by the author. One night in five at first, one in two and a half once the army has learned to fear you.
Ten points above the shipped curve. Silence is rare and the army finds you on most nights once Attention starts climbing.
Twenty five points above the shipped curve. At high Attention nearly every rest is interrupted. Resting becomes a decision instead of a habit.

World
Rewards
Ambushes

Warbands that spawn close and steal your first round. One event in five is an ambush. Turned off, that share becomes an ordinary patrol you can see coming, and no encounter anywhere grants a surprise round. Be aware of the limit: in Acts 2 and 3 the encounter tables do not separate patrol from ambush, so a few warbands can still start closer than a patrol would, they just cannot catch you flat-footed any more.
Additional tadpole specimens

True Souls and commanders of the Absolute carry a jar with a live tadpole, which drops when they die. There are 54 such carriers across the campaign. Turned off, no jar is ever placed, and the only tadpoles you find are the ones the base game gives you. Carriers already dead or already on the map keep what they were given.
Attention growth

Attention is the one-way meter that measures how seriously the Absolute takes you. It rises when you kill a commander, and it drives everything: how often you are found, which feats the troops get, when elites and the doctrine appear. This changes how fast the meter climbs, never where the tiers sit, so the whole escalation stays in shape.
Slow
Two dead commanders per step instead of one. The army takes about twice as long to reach its worst, and the progress you have made toward the next step is kept in your save.
Standard
One dead commander, one step. The curve the author tuned and shipped.
Fast
Two steps per dead commander. You reach elites, doctrine and the hardest bands in half the kills. Recommended only if you already know the escalation.
Commander rewards

What a dead commander leaves behind, on 117 commanders across the campaign. Troops are not affected: they keep their own light loot either way. One thing to know before you choose: the treasure is rolled when the commander SPAWNS, not when it dies, so a commander already standing in your world keeps whatever it was given, and the change reaches only the ones that appear next.
None
No bonus treasure at all. Commanders drop only the gear they are wearing. For a run where the fight is the reward.
Reduced
The lighter vanilla combat table. Gold and the occasional consumable, without the level-scaled scrolls and gems.
Standard
The shipped balance: the rich vanilla combat table, scaled to level. Gold, alchemy, special arrows, a scroll and gems.

Doctrine
Silencer

A caster sent specifically to shut yours down. It arrives once you have cast 15 spells in combat, and stops being sent if that count falls below 8. It carries Silence and Counterspell and opens by silencing the ground you stand on. Turned off, the role is never assigned; everything else the warband does is unchanged.
Markwarden

A bodyguard bound to the commander by Warding Bond: the commander takes half the damage and the warden bleeds the other half. It arrives once you have killed 3 commanders while their marked troops were still alive, and stops below 2. Turned off, commanders stand alone.
Doppelganger

If one of your characters does most of the killing, the army builds a copy of that character and sends it against you, with the same class, the same kit and the same level. It arrives after 3 such encounters and stops below 1. Turned off, no mirror is ever built.
Dynamic resistance

Hit the army 15 times with the same damage type and the next warbands arrive resistant to it. It holds at most 2 types at once, and each fades on its own over encounters where you stop using it. Turned off, no warband is ever granted resistance, and the ones already carrying it keep it until they die.
Feat ladder

The one growth that does not answer your style: it climbs with Attention alone. Watchful at Attention 2, Alert at 3, elite kits at 4 and 5. It is what puts Watchful on a warband you meet in the street. Turned off, every unit fights with the statline of its own template and nothing is ever added. Units already carrying a feat keep it.
Camp raids

The army finds the camp itself. Once Attention reaches 2, one long rest in seven is interrupted by a warband walking in among the bedrolls, drawn from the same tables as any other encounter and scaled to your level. The rest still completes: the night always ends, on three independent paths, even if the warband never arrives. Ships turned OFF, because an earlier version of this could trap a rest, and it is opt-in until it has proven itself in your campaign.
